newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Opposition ready to rejoin Central African govt.
newsitem.headline: Opposition ready to rejoin Central African govt.

text.p: Eleven opposition parties which suspended their participation in the government of the Central African Republic in May said they were now prepared to rejoin.

In a statement issued late on Thursday after a meeting, the "Group of 11" said their eight former ministers, who left the cabinet in protest at the killing of three disaffected soldiers, would accept a return to government.
Prime Minister Jean-Paul Ngoumpande is to suggest how this could be done to President Ange-Felix Patasse.
The soldiers, who had taken part in a series of mutinies in 1996, were killed by security forces in unexplained circumstances.

An attempt to reintegrate the mutineers into their regiments at the start of the year failed. At least 100 people were killed in further clashes in June between mutinous soldiers and members of an African peacekeeping force.

The United Nations Security Council on August 6 endorsed a continuing role for the peacekeepers and authorised the use of force to ensure respect of agreements aimed at ending the mutinies, which started as pay disputes before turning political.
